objective:
/goal Bring the native hyperboloidal N12 implementation to at least the performance of the previous implementation on two Aurora nodes, while preserving AthenaK’s native infrastructure and following the efficient execution patterns of Cartesian Z4c.

Work in the isolated hyperboloidal_cleaned_up branch. Keep production untouched. Inspect the current worktree, existing results, and pending changes before proceeding; preserve uncommitted work and existing scientific evidence.

Scope and success criterion
- Target two nodes / 24 GPU-tile ranks.
- Establish a matched N12 baseline for the previous implementation on those same resources. The historical 48-rank N12 timing and previous N24 timings are context, not acceptance targets.
- Use the fastest previously validated applicable implementation as the reference, preserving the same N12 physics and numerical workload.
- Success requires the native implementation’s median complete-RK4-step time to be no worse than the reference, with repeated measurements sufficient to distinguish improvement from noise.
- Do not expand this goal into eight-node optimization, a new resolution campaign, or further long evolution.
- Use existing validated saved states and short checkpoint continuations. Completion of the remaining fresh trajectory through 5 M is not a prerequisite for these bounded performance experiments.

Preserve the architecture
- Retain the original AthenaK Driver, TaskList machinery, MeshBlock/MeshBlockPack ownership, native tree, load balancing, restart/output infrastructure, and SMR/AMR support.
- Keep equal block weights.
- Keep surface state and treatment local to the ranks owning the outer MeshBlocks.
- Study the actual Cartesian Z4c implementation and reuse its useful kernel decomposition, data-access, boundary-exchange, and scheduling patterns.
- Do not introduce a replacement driver, parallel mesh hierarchy, custom scheduler, or globally replicated evolution state.
- Reuse existing infrastructure where its indexing and mathematical contracts fit; justify necessary mapped-grid extensions.

Establish trustworthy measurements first
1. Verify that the previous and native runs start from equivalent physical states, with restart conversion/mapping checked where formats differ.
2. Match compiler and floating-point policy, precision, GPU binding, grid, timestep, equations, KO=0.1, chi floor=1e-10, constant shift-speed policy, and boundary conditions.
3. Separate the stage observer’s overhead from the native solver’s cost using matched bounded controls.
4. Measure complete RK4 steps with detailed profiling disabled, warmup, repeated timing windows, and maximum-rank elapsed time. Report startup and diagnostic/I/O costs separately.
5. Profile representative bulk-heavy and surface-owning ranks to identify the actual critical path, GPU utilization, memory/register pressure, synchronization, and MPI progress. Do not infer the critical path by summing unrelated phase maxima.

Explore the following issues one at a time, reordering only when measurements justify it:

1. Bulk GPU kernel organization
   - Investigate the monolithic per-point reconstruction/RHS/KO kernel.
   - Compare with Cartesian Z4c’s separation of geometry, connection, gauge, and KO work.
   - Test field-parallel KO, endpoint radial reconstruction batching, and workgroup sizing as separate changes.
   - Check whether reduced per-thread live state actually improves complete-step time.
   - Avoid indiscriminate kernel splitting, large intermediate caches, or forced inlining without evidence.

2. Repeated geometry and overly general arithmetic
   - Reuse identical evolved-metric geometry within a point/stage evaluation.
   - Introduce value-only operations where projection or closure does not require full derivative jets.
   - Distinguish static coordinate geometry from evolved geometry; do not cache evolving quantities across stages.
   - Preserve the chi-guard and Penrose-geometry dependencies.

3. Surface execution
   - Evaluate batching the four independent normal-compatibility cases, followed by a separate small elimination kernel.
   - Precompute geometry-dependent angular interpolation weights and reuse them across components.
   - Consider a minimal compatibility-defect evaluator or analytic matrix only after establishing a measured baseline.
   - Retain the earlier analytic-matrix slowdown as evidence; do not assume fewer operations will be faster.
   - Preserve every surface, angular, radial-reconstruction, and normal-correction dependency.

4. Synchronization and task overlap
   - Measure host-returning reductions, observer collectives, packing fences, and MPI progress.
   - Consolidate checks at safe dependency boundaries and remove closure/projection passes only when their redundancy is proved.
   - Preserve required validity checks and prevent invalid intermediate states from being consumed.
   - Demonstrate actual communication/computation overlap rather than assuming nonblocking MPI provides it.

5. Communication and data layout
   - Investigate duplicate physical/residual donor exchange and reconstruction of residuals before interpolation.
   - Examine packing order, memory coalescing, reference/jet layout, and unnecessary data movement.
   - Reuse native Bvals for compatible routes only when correctness and measured cost support it.
   - Do not assume full boundary slabs, fused donor loops, or fewer kernels are automatically faster.

6. Remaining imbalance
   - Measure which ranks determine elapsed time.
   - Preserve equal block weights and block-local surfaces.
   - Consider block subdivision or workload-layout changes only if earlier fixes are insufficient, preserving the same physical grid and numerical workload.

Experiment and correctness discipline
- Change one substantive factor at a time.
- Compare each candidate against both the unchanged native control and the previous-implementation baseline.
- Prefer bitwise agreement when arithmetic order is preserved. Otherwise use existing justified tolerances established before examining candidate results; never loosen gates to obtain a pass.
- Validate complete bulk and surface states, chi records, boundary compatibility, constraints, horizon diagnostics, and restart continuity as applicable.
- Use poisoned-workspace checks when changing dependencies or intermediate storage.
- Exercise relevant SMR/AMR cases when a change affects refined operators, communication, storage, or plan rebuilding.
- Do not omit necessary RHS work, disable physical terms, enlarge dt, reduce precision, change resolution, or count RK stages as complete updates.
- Use make -j64. Serialize Aurora allocations, use only the two nodes required by this goal, check the queue before submission, and leave unrelated campaigns untouched.

Commit policy
- Commit an optimization only after correctness passes and repeated complete-step measurements confirm a real improvement.
- Make each successful optimization a separate, reviewable commit.
- Record the concrete change, measured before/after performance, numerical validation, and relevant limitations.
- Reject or revert slower and inconclusive candidates while retaining concise experimental evidence.
- Keep necessary measurement infrastructure separate from optimization commits and label it accurately.
- Do not turn source cleanup or speculative redesign into claimed performance progress.

Deliverables
- A reproducible matched two-node N12 baseline and final comparison.
- An evidence-based account of the dominant bottlenecks.
- Separate validated commits for retained improvements.
- A concise table of accepted and rejected experiments.
- Confirmation that the final committed implementation preserves AthenaK’s architecture and required numerical behavior.
- An honest statement of whether two-node performance parity was achieved.

Proceed autonomously within this scope. Do not request approval for routine isolated experiments or validated commits. If performance parity is not achieved, keep pursuing the measured bottleneck; do not redefine success around infrastructure work or partial speedups.

requirements.required_evidence: Use existing isolated branch; production untouched; serialized2nodes24ranks, make-j64 and fresh queue checks.
Preserve Driver, TaskList, block ownership/tree/equal weights, restart/output, locality and SMR/AMR; follow actual Cartesian Z4c design.
Verify complete equivalent native/legacy restart state and meaningful metadata, physical parameters and all chi histories.
Qualify and measure fastest applicable previously validated implementation on N12/24ranks; no48rank or N24 substitution.
Matched normal/timed-normal/timed-observer complete-state and diagnostic controls identify observer overhead.
Repeated warmed max-rank whole-RK4 windows, profiling off, same compiler/FP/grid/dt/physics; separate startup and diagnostics/I/O.
Profile representative bulk/surface owners and actual GPU/register/memory/synchronization/MPI progress; do not sum unrelated maxima.
Evaluate monolithic kernel, Cartesian Z4c decomposition, KO/radial batching and workgroups with measured evidence.
Evaluate repeated stage-local geometry/value-only arithmetic without invalid across-stage caching or altered chi/Penrose dependencies.
Evaluate case batching, static angular weights and minimal/analytic compatibility only when justified; retain earlier negative evidence.
Evaluate reductions, observer collectives, packing fences, closure redundancy and real overlap while preserving necessary checks.
Evaluate duplicate donor data, reconstruction before interpolation, layout/packing and appropriate native Bvals reuse.
Measure critical ranks while retaining equal weights and block-local surfaces; change workload layout only if justified and same physical work.
Complete bulk/surface/chi, compatibility, constraints, horizon and restart gates; poison and SMR/AMR tests where affected, no relaxed gates.
One factor at a time; separate optimization commits only for repeated accepted improvements; retain failures and revert slower/inconclusive changes.
Final committed native median no worse than fastest accepted old reference with sufficient repeatability; reproducible evidence, profiles, experiment table and architecture confirmation.
